verification.stockFirefoxChecks: Seven cases, native keyboard full forward/reverse, real-time replay and exact unchanged nine-store/local/session snapshots

conditions: Each matrix input uses an independent real document within the same browser context/DB; maximum size first, representative last.
All real executions finish before any playback clock is installed; six rate replays observe each adjacent rendered cursor and state from the same accepted trace.
Receive observer snapshots bytes with slice only; Base64 transport/Node byte arrays are created only after production acceptance/rejection.
Seven representative raw archives are immutable public developer evidence; all 42x3 captures remain separately available in .artifacts.
failureHistory: First unit round: noncanonical multi-field JSON key order in new tests; test encoder corrected, not product/Rust.
First stock Firefox script: selector quoting syntax; structured selector parameter fixed and failure retained.
First Chrome case suite: 1/9; new test waited for a settings-only status element. Corrected to actual case subject-loaded text.
Several 30-item reverse bubble runs reached original receive deadline; raw timing and results retained. Delayed getters did not alone resolve it; fresh documents alone also had one failure.
Final fixed conditions use independent documents and maximum input first; final 42x3 and full quality run passed without automatic retry or increased deadline.

knownLimitations.status: reproduced, unresolved under accumulated large-result workload
knownLimitations.detail: 5330-step / 7047287-byte reverse30 bubble result: observed Rust 523-630ms, reception/complete validation approached original1000ms. Slice2.3-4.5ms and byte getters after termination do not prove capture is the sole cause. No general repeated-large-result throughput or full performance claim.

evidenceBoundary: Only current unpublished contract-fixture preview has zero learning writes; this is not acceptance of 11.1 real first-view grants or cross-tab reward idempotency.
All results are actual Rust production Worker buffers; expected outputs and array facts are fixed public test data, never frontend C evaluation.
Maximum inputs are decoded/checked entirely, but only seven representatives traverse every UI cursor in both directions.
Full performance/accessibility/cold-warm/network/device matrix, publishing, exercises, blocks and phase11.5 remain outside this task.
